turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve been getting more confused lately and I can’t really put my thoughts into words. I also have a fever around 102°F and it’s uncomfortable when you press on my right upper belly.
Have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes?
I… I think my eyes or skin might look more yellow than usual, but I’m not entirely sure. My family has noticed changes, and I’ve been feeling more disoriented since the fever started.
Have your stools become pale or clay-colored, and has your urine become dark like tea or cola?

I don’t know for sure, but my family says my bowel movements have looked lighter than usual, and my urine seems darker than normal. I’ve been too disoriented to track it myself, but the fever and the right-upper belly discomfort started around the same time.
Have you felt dizzy, lightheaded, or noticed your blood pressure being low when checked recently?

Patient: I’ve felt very weak and lightheaded when I try to sit up, and I believe my blood pressure has been on the lower side when they checked, but I’m not sure of the exact numbers. I also get more confused after moving around.
Do you have a history of gallstones, prior gallbladder surgery, or other biliary problems?

I don’t recall any gallbladder surgery, but I’ve had “liver or gall” problems in the past—my family mentioned gallstones at one point, though I can’t confirm the details. I’ve been in hospice, and I’m not sure what treatments I had before for that.

“Doctor, yes—I’ve had weakness and I feel lightheaded when I try to move, and my confusion seems worse around that time. My family says my skin and eyes look more yellow, and they’ve noticed my stools are lighter and my urine is much darker since the fever began. I don’t know my exact past treatments or whether I definitely had gallstones, but I have had liver or gall-related issues before.”
Do you have a known diagnosis of cancer, particularly involving the liver, pancreas, or bile ducts?

Patient: I don’t know of any diagnosed cancer involving my liver, pancreas, or bile ducts—at least I haven’t been told that. I’ve been in hospice mainly for a chronic illness, but I can’t recall the specific diagnosis or names of treatments I received before.
Have you taken any acetaminophen (Tylenol) or other pain medications recently, and if so, how much?
I’ve had some pain and fever meds, but I don’t know the names or exact doses—my family or hospice staff usually give them. I can’t reliably say whether it was acetaminophen versus something else.
Have you experienced shaking chills or rigors with the fever?
I’ve had chills along with the fever—my body shakes and I feel like I can’t stop shivering, especially when the temperature spikes. I don’t know if you’d call them rigors, but it feels quite intense.
[DDX] Acute suppurative cholangitis (Reynolds' pentad), Acute cholecystitis with choledocholithiasis, Pyogenic liver abscess, Severe acute hepatitis, Sepsis with secondary hepatic dysfunction
